item.title: Iran-Aligned Volant Manticore Uses IPFS-Based KuboShell Backdoor in Espionage Campaigns
item.description: A previously undocumented Iran-aligned cyber espionage group called Volant Manticore has targeted telecommunications companies, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus. Central to the group's operations is a backdoor called KuboShell that uses the InterPlanetary File System ( IPFS ) for command-and-control (C2) and deploys Homa, a post-compromise framework that's a reimplementation of MuddyWater's MuddyC2Go . Evidence indicates that the threat actor has been operational since late August 2025. Also delivered alongside these tools are Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) programs like MeshCentral and NetLock RMM. In tandem, the group has been observed orchestrating credential harvesting campaigns to collect email and corporate credentials of some of the impersonated organizations. item.title: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap
item.description: Pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version of their code, known as SHA pinning, has become the go-to defense against software supply chain attacks. Attackers have already found a way around it. In March 2026, the hackers who hijacked Trivy, a widely used open-source security scanner, planted malicious code that looked like it came from GitHub's official checkout tool. They even labeled it a security fix. Teams pinned to it would have passed every check. The trick works because GitHub lets copies of a project, called forks, share code with the original. In May, the same technique hit the popular actions-cool/issues-helper tool, stealing credentials from the pipelines that ran it. The lesson: pinning guarantees the code won't change, but not who wrote it. That gap is the focus of an upcoming webinar, GitHub Actions Security Beyond SHA Pinning . If your team treats pinning as the finish line, save your seat to learn what it actually protects you from, and what it doesn...

item.title: Google Researcher Shows How a Single Bit Change in .NET Files Bypassed Windows Code Integrity
item.description: A quirk in how the .NET Framework loads a program file let a local attacker run untrusted code past two separate protections on Windows built to block it, Google Project Zero researcher James Forshaw showed in a write-up published yesterday. The same loading behavior bypassed Oracle VirtualBox's process hardening on Windows hosts, tracked as CVE-2026-87268 , and Windows code integrity, tracked as CVE-2026-108398 . Oracle fixed the VirtualBox flaw in September, and Microsoft fixed the Windows one on October 13, both before the write-up appeared. VirtualBox on Windows monitors the system calls that load program files into its virtual machine processes, so a less-trusted user on the same computer cannot push code into them. Forshaw got past that watch through the .NET Framework. The framework can run a .NET program file from a plain copy in memory when the normal way of loading it, as an executable image, fails. item.title: 2027 SOC Budget Reset: 5 Priorities to Cut Costs and Reduce Cyber Risk
item.description: What if your biggest SOC budget problem isn't how much you spend, but how much analyst time you lose? According to ANY.RUN 's estimates, SOC teams could recover 450 analyst hours per 1,000 investigated alerts through faster threat analysis and IOC research. That's a significant opportunity as manual investigations, repeated checks, and unnecessary escalations continue to drain resources. As 2027 approaches, here are five priorities to reduce SOC costs, recover capacity, and strengthen protection against costly cyberattacks. Why 2027 SOC Budget Planning Is Getting More Challenging Cybersecurity spending is facing conflicting pressures. According to IANS and Artico Search, 55% of CISOs reported flat or declining budgets in 2026 . Meanwhile, PwC's 2027 Global Digital Trust Insights found that 84% of surveyed security and finance leaders expect cybersecurity budgets to increase .

No login is needed. The company disclosed the SQL injection yesterday along with two other flaws that need a logged-in client, and released fixed versions. The development comes as AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery, finding critical bugs in foundational software used to power internet-connected software.
